study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Sayantan Kumar et al., Alzheimer's & Dementia, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Analyzing heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease using multimodal normative modeling on imaging-based ATN biomarkers

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To identify individual patterns of neuroanatomical and neuropathological variation in Alzheimer's Disease (AD) brains using a deep learning-based normative modeling framework on multimodal amyloid-tau-neurodegeneration (ATN) imaging biomarkers.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper clearly states the two datasets used for the discovery and replication cohorts.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We constructed a discovery dataset consisting of individuals from ADNI and a replication dataset consisting of individuals from the Charles F. and Joanne Knight ADRC dataset at Washington University in St. Louis.

rci5_imaging_modality.answer: T1-weighted MRI; Amyloid PET ([18F]Florbetapir); Tau PET ([18F]-Flortaucipir)
rci5_imaging_modality.reason: The paper describes the use of these three modalities for all participants in the analysis. It explicitly mentions T1-weighted MRI, and PET for amyloid and tau, specifying the tracers used.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: For both datasets, participants were required to have T1weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), as well as amyloid and tau positron emission tomography (PET) imaging... To avoid harmonization issues due to multiple tracers, we only included data collected using FBPin our analyses for both ADNI and Knight ADRC... Tau-PET imaging was performed using FTP.

rci6_analysis_level.supporting_text: The final data included in our analyses (both ADNI and Knight ADRC) included pre-processed regional grey matter volumes of 66 cortical ROIs (33 per hemisphere) and 24 subcortical ROIs for each participant.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: ADNI: FreeSurfer v6.0, Desikan-Killiany atlas, Aseg atlas; Knight ADRC: FreeSurfer v5.3, Desikan-Killiany atlas, Aseg atlas, PET Unified Pipeline (PUP).
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper explicitly mentions the software and atlases used for preprocessing for both cohorts.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: The T1-weighted sequences from ADNI and Knight ADRC were preprocessed using FreeSurfer versions 6 and 5.3, respectively. The cortical surface of each hemisphere was parcellated according to the Desikan-Killiany atlas... and anatomical region of interest (ROI) measures were obtained via a whole-brain segmentation procedure (Aseg atlas)... All PET images from Knight ADRC (FBP and FTP) were processed using the PET Unified Pipeline (https:// github.com/ysu001/PUP).

rci8_quality_checking.detail: ADRC: For images failing a quality control check, the preprocessing pipeline was rerun. Details on specific metrics or exclusion numbers are not provided.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: For all images failing a quality control check, the processing pipeline was rerun to ensure consistency across all scans.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: The paper describes a transfer learning approach to handle differences between the two sites/datasets. This is a form of site effect handling, but doesn't fit neatly into 'Batch-removal' or 'Model-based'. The study used two separate datasets (discovery and replication). For the replication dataset (ADRC), the model pre-trained on the discovery set (ADNI) was fine-tuned via transfer learning to account for dataset-specific biases.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: For replication in the Knight ADRC dataset, mmVAE pretrained on ADNI-CU-train underwent fine-tuning on ADRC-CU-tl through transfer learning..." and "Although we fine-tuned our pre-trained normative model on the replication cohort to address dataset-specific biases...
rci9_site_effect_handling.location: Kumar2025.pdf.md: 2.5.1 Model training, 4.4 Limitations and scope for future work

nm1_model_origin.detail: The paper states they used a 'previously validated' framework, but they trained it from scratch on the ADNI-CU-train set. It is not a pre-trained model in the sense of applying a model trained on a different, massive dataset. The guide says 'For New: set Detail to '-'. -
nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: Initially, mmVAE was trained using the ADNI-CU-train set... For replication in the Knight ADRC dataset, mmVAE pretrained on ADNI-CU-train underwent fine-tuning on ADRC-CU-tl through transfer learning

nm2_modeling_method.reason: The paper clearly and repeatedly states the use of a multimodal variational autoencoder (mmVAE).
nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: This framework is based on a multimodal variational autoencoder (mmVAE), which takes as input cross-sectional ATN biomarker data including regional gray matter volumes, as well as amyloid FBP and tau FTP SUVR values

nm3_software_tool.reason: The paper mentions Python and ggseg for analysis and visualization. It does not specify the deep learning library (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) used to build the mmVAE model.
nm3_software_tool.supporting_text: All analyses were performed using Python 3.7. All visualizations of the brain atlases for the effect size maps... were visualized using the python package ggseg.

nm4_response_variable.answer: Regional grey matter volumes (66 cortical, 24 subcortical ROIs), regional amyloid FBP SUVR values (66 cortical, 24 subcortical ROIs), and regional tau FTP SUVR values (66 cortical, 24 subcortical ROIs).
nm4_response_variable.reason: The paper clearly defines the input variables for the model, which are reconstructed, making them the response variables in the autoencoder context.
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: ...mmVAE... takes as input cross-sectional ATN biomarker data including regional gray matter volumes, as well as amyloid FBP and tau FTP SUVR values... the final amyloidFBP and tau-FTP data included in our analyses from both ADNI and Knight ADRC consisted of regional standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) values for 66 cortical ROIs (33 per hemisphere) and 24 subcortical ROIs for each participant.

nm5_predictor_variables.reason: The paper states the model was conditioned on age and sex. In a normative model, these are the predictors used to model the expected distribution.
nm5_predictor_variables.supporting_text: mmVAE was conditioned on the age and sex of participants to remove the effect of covariates

nm6_predictor_effects.answer: Predictor effects (age and sex) were handled by conditioning the decoder networks on one-hot encoded vectors of these covariates.
nm6_predictor_effects.reason: The supplementary material explains that age and sex were one-hot encoded and fed into the decoder part of the VAE. This is a specific way of accounting for their effects, rather than a typical fixed/random effect in a regression model.
nm6_predictor_effects.supporting_text: Both age and sex were transformed into one-hot encoding vectors... Both the modality-specific decoders used these vectors together with the latent code to reconstruct the brain data.

nm7_nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The model explicitly handles age and sex by conditioning. It addresses site effects through a train/fine-tune (transfer learning) approach on a separate replication cohort. It addresses the non-Gaussian nature and heteroscedasticity of brain data implicitly by using a VAE to learn the entire data distribution.
nm7_nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: mmVAE was conditioned on the age and sex of participants to remove the effect of covariates... For replication in the Knight ADRC dataset, mmVAE pretrained on ADNI-CU-train underwent fine-tuning on ADRC-CU-tl through transfer learning...

nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not report validation metrics (like model fit, explained variance, etc.) on the training data itself (ADNI-CU-train). The validation focuses entirely on hold-out and test sets.

nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study uses a train/validation/test split (75:15:10) within the main ADNI-CU cohort. The validation set is used for standardizing Z-scores, and the test set is used as a baseline control group for statistical comparisons, which constitutes validation on an independent, same-domain dataset.
nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: The ADNI-CU group was further divided into a training set for model training (ADNI-CU-train; n = 326), a holdout validation set (ADNI-CU-holdout; n = 65), and a test set (ADNI-CU-test; n = 43) at a ratio of 75:15:10... The validation set was used to standardize deviations of ADNI-ADS and calculate Z -scores relative to ADNI-CU. The test sets served as a baseline control group to compare statistics of ADS individuals against amyloid-negative CU participants.

nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The entire study's findings were replicated on a separate, independent dataset (Knight ADRC). The model was fine-tuned (transfer learning) on the ADRC controls and then applied to the ADRC disease group, and all key results are shown to be reproducible.
nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: The results were replicated in an independent dataset, part of the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer's Disease Research Center (ADRC) dataset at Washington University in St. Louis.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-score; Binary abnormality map; Disease Severity Index (DSI)
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper describes a multi-step process: calculating regional deviations, normalizing them to Z-scores, creating binary maps based on a threshold (Z<-1.96 for MRI, Z>1.96 for PET), and then computing a composite Disease Severity Index (DSI) from these.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: This step generated regional, modality-specific Z -score deviations... For MRI gray matter volumes, regional Z -scores below -1.96... were labeled as abnormal... For each ADS individual, we created a binary thresholded abnormality map... every individual's DSI was calculated by (i) first performing an inner product between the binary thresholded abnormality map (Section 2.6.1) and the regional deviation vector; and (ii) then normalizing the inner product by the total number of regions...
caa6_deviation_metric.location: Kumar2025.pdf.md: 2.5.3 Normalizing deviations into Z-scores, 2.6.1 Regional abnormal deviations across ATN biomarkers, 2.6.5 DSI across ADS groups

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group differences in regional deviations were assessed with Cohen's d. Intra-group heterogeneity was measured with Hamming distance and compared across groups. Associations between the Disease Severity Index (DSI) and cognitive composites (memory, executive function, language) were tested with linear regression, adjusted for age and sex. The relationship between DSI and clinical progression (conversion to CDR >= 1) was examined using survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier plots, log-rank tests), adjusted for age and sex.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Using a multimodal normative model, the study identified heterogeneous patterns of atrophy, amyloid, and tau deposition in Alzheimer's disease, with greater heterogeneity in more severe dementia stages, and developed a Disease Severity Index (DSI) that correlates with cognitive impairment and progression risk.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found heterogeneous patterns of abnormal deviations across gray matter, amyloid, and tau in AD patients. Intra-group dissimilarity (heterogeneity) increased with dementia severity (CDR stages), with MRI showing more spatial variation than tau or amyloid. A multimodal Disease Severity Index (DSI) was developed which increased with dementia severity and was significantly associated with impaired memory (r=-0.62 in ADNI, r=-0.68 in ADRC), executive function, and language. Higher DSI was also significantly associated with a faster progression to a clinical dementia rating of 1 or greater in longitudinal analysis.

caa10_key_limitations.answer:
1. Use of cross-sectional data makes it difficult to distinguish disease stages from subtypes.
2. Demographic differences between cohorts and lack of diversity (both cohorts are from North America) limit generalizability.
3. Different processing software versions (FreeSurfer 6 vs 5.3) and scanners between cohorts could introduce variability.
4. The study did not include imaging biomarkers for cerebrovascular disease, an important co-pathology.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, we used cross-sectional imaging data for our normative modeling framework... Second, Demographic differences between the ADNI and Knight ADRC cohorts... Third, the imaging scans in the discovery and replication cohorts were processed with different versions of FreeSurfer... Finally, cerebrovascular disease burden is an important copathology in AD... we acknowledge that vascular burden represents an essential dimension to understand AD.
caa10_key_limitations.location: Kumar2025.pdf.md: 4.4 Limitations and scope for future work

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study developed a composite Disease Severity Index (DSI) that integrates the spatial extent and magnitude of abnormal deviations across three imaging modalities (MRI, amyloid PET, tau PET) into a single, personalized metric of brain health.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study presents a comprehensive analysis using a novel multimodal deep learning framework (mmVAE) to characterize heterogeneity in Alzheimer's disease across two independent cohorts (ADNI and Knight ADRC). A key contribution is the development of a Disease Severity Index (DSI) which integrates atrophy, amyloid, and tau data. The model was trained on one cohort and validated on the other using transfer learning, demonstrating the robustness of the findings.
